segments.text: Criminal justice is the institutional system through which crime is investigated, prosecuted, adjudicated and sanctioned.

The system is a chain: police investigation → prosecution → courts → corrections, with probation/parole and informal/community mechanisms at different points. Weakness at one stage can affect the entire process.

blocks.text: A system rather than isolated institutions

segments.text: The criminal justice system is a chain of institutions and decisions: reporting and detection → investigation → prosecutorial screening → charge → trial or lawful disposition → sentence → corrections → release and reintegration. A failure at one stage can affect every later stage, so coordination and accountability are systemic issues.

Formal agencies include police, prosecution, courts, prisons, probation and parole structures. Informal mechanisms—family, community leadership, civil society and social services—may influence prevention and reintegration but do not automatically possess legal coercive powers.

Police prevent, detect and investigate crime within statutory powers. Prosecutors assess evidence, conduct the state’s case and are expected to act within duties of fairness and law. Courts determine legal questions, protect due process and decide guilt and sentence on the basis of admissible evidence and applicable standards.
These roles should remain institutionally distinct. Investigation is not conviction, accusation is not proof, and prosecution does not make the court’s final determination.

Prisons carry out custodial sentences and detention under law; modern correctional policy also addresses safety, health, rehabilitation and release planning. The UN Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, revised in 2015 and known as the Nelson Mandela Rules, provide internationally recognized minimum standards for prison treatment.

Probation supervises eligible offenders in the community under conditions. Parole is conditional release after part of a custodial sentence where the legal system provides it. Both require risk management, support and clear consequences for violations.

items.text: Criminal justice is a chain of institutions. Police investigate, prosecutors assess and present cases, courts determine guilt and sentence, and correctional agencies execute lawful sanctions.
Probation and parole are community-based mechanisms but operate at different stages and under different legal conditions. They should not be treated as synonyms.
Formal agencies exercise powers created by law; informal institutions such as families, communities and civil society also influence prevention, reporting and reintegration.
System performance depends on coordination. Delay, poor investigation, weak prosecution, prison overcrowding or inadequate rehabilitation at one stage can undermine outcomes elsewhere.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not analyze each institution in isolation. Explain how a failure at one point can affect fairness and effectiveness across the entire justice chain.

items.text: Prepare functions and common institutional problems separately.
Use process diagrams and reform-oriented analysis.

Coordination and due process are both essential.
